newsitem.title: GERMANY: Anzag has strong earnings in last 4 months.
newsitem.headline: Anzag has strong earnings in last 4 months.

text.p: German pharmaceutical wholesaler Andreae-Noris Zahn AG (Anzag) on Thursday reported strong earnings in the first four months of its business year despite difficult conditions in its home market.

"During the first four months of the current business year we managed to earn more than we did during the same time last year even though our sales were lower," Anzag management board chairman Hermann Franke told a news conference.
He declined to give more details.

The group also reported that net profit for the 1995/1996 business year, ending August 31, jumped 19 percent to 38.5 million marks. During the same time sales climbed 6.3 percent to 4.3 billion marks.
Franke said the group's success is largely based on its decision to concentrate on the German market, stopping all plans to expand into eastern Europe, particularly into Poland.
"Our direction is clearly the right one for our customers, shareholders and employees," Franke said.
The group's strong results helped it raise its 1995/1996 dividend payout by 28 percent to 18 marks per share.

This spring the group plans to reduce the nominal value of its shares to five marks from 50 marks, following a broad trend among German companies eager to attract private investors to the share market.

German pharmaceutical companies and by extension wholesalers have said that the country's restrictive drugs budget, setting a limit the total cost of drugs physicians may prescribe, has weighed on business conditions.
